items.title: Critical Flaw in Python’s Popular Pillow Image Library Allows Code Execution via a Crafted Image
items.summary: Pillow, the most widely used image library for Python, can be made to run operating system commands on a server by specifying the name of a file it is told to open. The flaw, CVE-2026-112900, is in the way Pillow handles EPS images, which it opens by passing the file's name to Gh
items.author: Swati Khandelwal

items.summary: Malicious Brotli data can make an application on an official build of Node.js run attacker-supplied code, security researchers at Imperva have demonstrated. Their "Node2Shell" proof of concept ran code on the official Node.js 24.22.0 image for Linux arm64, with no debugger or cus
items.author: Swati Khandelwal

items.title: Critical x402 SDK Flaw Could Let Malicious APIs Drain AI Agents’ Token Balances
items.summary: AI agents paying for API calls with the x402 SDKs could sign a payment for their full balance of a supported token if a malicious API asked for it, security firm V12 said on October 22. The cause was the SDKs' default client, which set no spending limit until releases on August 1
items.author: Swati Khandelwal
